summary: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy was used to screen 17 metal and nitride capping layers on 60 nm Nb films for their ability to prevent oxygen diffusion through standard fabrication steps: annealing at 200 °C, AZ 300T resist stripping, and acid cleaning (2% HF, 10:1 BOE, Nanostrip). Resonator measurements on down-selected caps (Ta, TaN, TiN, Zr) showed Ta and TaN-capped samples achieve lower medium-power loss $\delta_{\mathrm{MP}}$ than bare Nb control, with Ta and TaN resilient to all tested processes while most other metals suffered oxidation or etching.
motivation: Surface oxides of superconducting Nb are a major source of loss in qubits and resonators. Understanding how capping layers protect the Nb-oxide interface during fabrication—annealing, resist stripping, and acid cleaning—is essential for integrating effective encapsulation strategies into device processing.
method: Bilayers of 60 nm Nb with 5 nm caps (Al, Au, Hf, Mo, Pd, Pt, Ta, Ti, W, Zr, Ti-W, Zr-Y, plus NbN, HfN, TaN, TiN, ZrN) were deposited in-situ on high-resistivity Si wafers. Samples underwent annealing (200 °C, 1 h in air or vacuum), AZ 300T strip bath, or acid dips, then analyzed by XPS measuring Nb oxidation state from electrons escaping the top 5–10 nm. Resonators were fabricated from promising caps and measured at 500 mK to extract $\delta_{\mathrm{MP}}$ ($\langle n \rangle < 100$ photons) and $\delta_{\mathrm{HP}}$ ($\langle n \rangle > 10^6$ photons).
result: Ta and TaN caps prevented Nb oxidation after annealing, strip bath, and all acid cleans. Ta-capped resonators achieved $\delta_{\mathrm{MP}}$ lower than control Nb; TaN similarly reduced $\delta_{\mathrm{MP}}$. Noble metals (Au, Pd, Pt) failed as barriers, allowing Nb oxidation after air annealing. Mo, W, and Ti-W were eroded by the AZ 300T strip; Al, Hf, Zr were damaged by all acid treatments.
